I am an old man now, 72 years, and my strength is not what it was. This small piece of land near the house, only half an acre, I keep for beans because beans do not need the chemical fertilizer like maize does — they feed themselves from the soil. I have no money to buy the fertilizer from the shop, so I will put the manure from my goats and chickens, and I will save seeds from last year's harvest like my father taught me. My wife and my grown children will help me weed, because at my age I cannot bend all day in the sun.
